title: Jimmy Kimmel reacts to Trump posting an AI video of himself wrestling a tiger
body: We regret to inform you that the president has been posting AI videos again . In the late night clip above, Jimmy Kimmel recaps Trump's latest slop post of himself chasing and wrestling a tiger , before appearing to befriend it. "To me the most unrealistic part of that video is him running," says Kimmel. "I guess maybe he's bored? How can you be president and be bored? If you want to know how brave he really is around wild animals, this is from a photo shoot he did with an eagle." Cue some (real) footage from 10 years ago of Trump flinching away from a bald eagle during a photoshoot. "He would definitely suplex a tiger," says Kimmel. The AI video is bizarre when viewed by itself, but it gets worse when you add in context. Prior to sharing the AI footage, Trump posted a clip of a British man, William Chapman, inside a tiger enclosure video that was taken moments before he was killed on Saturday. Chapman's family has called the circulation of the footage "deeply offensive", and said it's causing them "severe distress". Want more of the best of late night? body: When you think of the Friday the 13th franchise, you think of Jason Voorhees, his hockey mask, and his perpetually bloody machete. But never forget that the original slasher in the first Friday the 13th was actually Jason's mother, Camp Crystal Lake cook Pamela Voorhees. Now, Pam takes center stage in Peacock and A24's prequel series Crystal Lake , in which she's played by Emmy winner Linda Cardellini. SEE ALSO: 2026 fall TV preview: Every show you should know about What's Crystal Lake about? Credit: Matt Infante / Peacock Crystal Lake revisits classic moments of the Friday the 13th mythology through Pam's eyes. We witness firsthand her grief at Jason's (Callum Vinson) drowning, and the rage that sparks her later killing spree. Notably, showrunner Brad Caleb Kane ( IT: Welcome to Derry ) moves the timeline up so that Jason drowns in 1971 as opposed to 1957. Much of Crystal Lake will feel familiar to anyone who's watched Friday the 13th . The series mimics the film's title sequence, POV killer shots, and score, while also managing to capture the summery vibes of Camp Crystal Lake. However, it also conjures up an entirely new backstory for Pam, one that begins to come to light when two strangers show up at her house, ready to ask her questions about her past and spirit her away. Of course, Pam fights back, resulting in the first of many bloody kills for Mama Voorhees. It's an invigorating sequence, complete with a gnarly set piece I can only describe as "blood balloon." title: Artificial review: Andrew Garfield enters his villain era
body: When much of the world looks at Andrew Garfield, they see a hero. Not only has the charismatic English actor played Spider-Man, but he's also been the noble protagonist of The Uprising , Under the Banner of Heaven, Silence, and tick, tick Boom! Yet when Italian film director Luca Guadagnino looks at Garfield, he sees that the actor's potential as a villain lies in his charms. Last year, with After the Hunt , Guadagnino employed Garfield's sex appeal to set up a flirty academic who is then accused of sexual assault. The audience's presumed appreciation for Garfield scratches us in this role, as we're asked to consider if such a beguiling man could be a rapist. Now, with Artificial , Guadagnino weaponizes Garfield's charms more extensively. Together, they portray OpenAI cofounder Sam Altman as a cult leader, and by extension the artificial intelligence industry as a cult desperate for all of us to, if not join, then at least submit. SEE ALSO: 'The AI Doc' director says F*ck you to AI companies stealing artists IP Artificial centers on the rise of OpenAI, but not Sam Altman. The controversial AI exec is a sly antagonist in Artificial. The film itself follows Ilya Sutskever ( Anora 's Yura Borisov), a Soviet-born computer scientist who was making waves with his research in Canada when Altman came knocking. In Ilya, Artificial presents an idealist who is drawn in by Sam's argument that OpenAI is not a company built to prioritize profits over the well-being of mankind. title: Flock CEO says it wont work with clients who abuse its surveillance, but claims none have
body: Flock CEO Garrett Langley has stated that the controversial surveillance company would "immediately" stop partnering with any clients who abused its systems , including law enforcement agencies. However, he also claimed that Flock has not yet found any cause to do so, arguing that all incidents thus far have been the fault of a small number of bad actors within organisations. SEE ALSO: An officer's use of Flock cameras was 'unconstitutional,' judge rules Speaking at TechCrunch Disrupt on Wednesday, Langley attempted to allay widespread concerns that Flock could be facilitating mass surveillance and violations of privacy. There have been multiple instances of U.S. law enforcement officials being charged with abusing Flock's system, using it to stalk, harass, and surveil people without just cause. However, Flock has not cancelled its partnerships with any clients, Langley taking the view that such incidents were due to individual actors within organisations. "Most of the debate is nuanced into 'what if two officers out of 50 were caught?'" said Langley. "Today, we haven't fired any customers, but it's not off the table in the case of some pretty drastic law-abiding issue." According to the public interest law firm Institute for Justice , there have been over 240 incidents of U.S. law enforcement abusing automated license plate readers such as Flock's since 2021. Many cases involve officers tracking women or former partners. body: Welcome to your guide to Pips, the latest game in the New York Times catalog. Released in August 2025, Pips puts a unique spin on dominoes, creating a fun single-player experience that could become your next daily gaming habit. How to play Pips If you've ever played dominoes, you'll have a passing familiarity with how Pips is played. As we've shared in our previous hints stories for Pips, the tiles, like dominoes, are placed vertically or horizontally and connect with each other. The main difference between a traditional game of dominoes and Pips is the color-coded conditions you have to address. The touching tiles don't necessarily have to match. SEE ALSO: Wordle today: Answer, hints for October 15, 2026 The conditions you have to meet are specific to the color-coded spaces. For example, if it provides a single number, every side of a tile in that space must add up to the number provided. It is possible and common for only half a tile to be within a color-coded space. body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. title: Is that singer even real? Music streaming services are starting to tell you.
body: You put on a playlist to find something good to listen to. Checking whether the singer exists wasn t supposed to be part of the process. But a song these days can fit your taste perfectly and still leave you wondering who, or what, made it. This week, two music streaming services Google s YouTube Music and the French platform Deezer announced features that could make that question easier to answer. YouTube Music is adding labels to AI-generated songs, while Deezer will let listeners filter fully AI-generated music out of search results. For listeners who have been opening artist profiles and hunting for evidence of an actual musician, that could mean considerably less homework. What s changing when you press play? YouTube says the new labels respond to something listeners have been asking for: "As these tools evolve, our listeners have told us they want transparency when they re hearing an AI-generated track," the company wrote. Starting Oct. 14, those labels will appear directly on YouTube Music s player for songs created primarily using generative AI, including generated compositions and vocals. Tapping the label opens more information about the track. YouTube says it is working with music partners and using its own detection tools to identify AI-generated songs, with the labels also coming to the main YouTube app. Credit: Screenshot: YouTube News Deezer is offering an additional choice: leave those songs out of your search altogether. title: Lawsuit alleges OpenAI stole childrens user data
body: A mother of two is suing OpenAI in a proposed class action lawsuit that alleges the company "stole" valuable data from millions of young users without their consent. The anonymous mother, whose children are 12 and 16, resides in Hawaii. Both children signed up for ChatGPT accounts in early 2026 without parental permission. OpenAI requires, but doesn't actively check, that a child has sought their parents' permission. Its terms of service prohibit minors younger than 13 from using ChatGPT, though many do regardless. SEE ALSO: Report: OpenAI should pause ChatGPT for Teens over safety The complaint alleges that ChatGPT "purposely extracted" sensitive personal information from both children, including emotional insecurities, relationship concerns, and selfies. It broadly argues that OpenAI "exploits" minor users through design features like speaking in first person, mirroring communication style, possessing memory to build on past chats, and being sycophantic, or overly flattering and agreeable. "For years, it wrongfully has extracted vast amounts of highly sensitive and valuable data from millions of children," the complaint says of OpenAI. "It had no right to take this information, but it took it anyway. It then used that priceless trove of children s information to train large language models, build detailed profiles of children, and enrich itself." OpenAI recently sought a valuation of $1.4 trillion as it prepares to go public, according to Bloomberg Law . title: Fridge hack costing millions and sparking fires stemmed from poor security
author: Dan Goodin
body: Earlier this week, a mass hack of refrigeration systems at an estimated 700 supermarkets throughout France caused them to suddenly malfunction, causing spoilage of untold tons of perishables and, in some cases, fires. As is now the norm, basic cybersecurity would have prevented it. French authorities say the systems, made up of entire fleets of refrigerators and freezers throughout a store, were hacked. More specifically, Internet-connected controllers that allow technicians to remotely administer the store-wide systems were compromised. The unknown attackers responsible then activated defrosters long enough for the fridges to reach temperatures as high as 50° Celsius (122° Fahrenheit). By the time the mass compromise was discovered, food was spoiled, and in some cases their electrical systems caught fire. The hacks that didn't have to happen Multiple security advisories and public research reports show that all three of the controller models reportedly hacked in the incident—sold by Danfoss of Denmark and Dixell and its parent company Copeland in the US—contained critical vulnerabilities that allow attackers to remotely log in to the devices with the same system rights as administrators. Until recently, Danfoss controllers, for instance, used a credential that changes each day. The password is generated by the publicly available firmware based on the date. A hacker who takes the time to analyze the code can do the same thing on any device that hasn’t received a recent update. title: Epic says its new vibe-coded Epic Games Launcher is faster than Steam
author: Kyle Orland
body: Nearly eight years after Epic took on Steam with its own Game Store and launcher, the Fortnite maker is deploying a new tool to give it an edge over Valve: vibe coding. In announcing the new publicly available "Preview" build of its Epic Games Launcher, Epic writes that "programming is hard. So, instead of doing that, we vibe coded a new Epic Games Launcher that’s way faster and more responsive than the current one, and has a new look." And while that might sound a little tongue-in-cheek, Epic Games Store General Manager and VP Martin Keely told PC Gamer that the team "started from scratch" and used AI as "a tool to write and review new features and new capabilities from the ground up in a different tech stack than what we had previously." The goal, Keely said, was to "look at functionality that existed [in the current Epic Games Launcher] and [say] we want to replicate that, but not the code itself." Speaking to IGN , Keely clarified that using AI to code the new Launcher "made us more efficient and allowed a small team to rewrite the code base and be able to launch it faster across platforms, support Windows and Mac, and we're going to have a Linux version as well." title: Things are finally looking up for NASA's first missions to Venus in a generation
author: Stephen Clark
body: Most planetary scientists will tell you the heyday of Venus exploration was more than a generation ago. That is about to change. Two NASA missions are on track to launch to Venus in the early 2030s. The first, known as the Deep Atmosphere Venus Investigation of Noble gases, Chemistry, and Imaging (DAVINCI), is now scheduled for launch in December 2030, a year earlier than previously planned. DAVINCI will send a parachute-assisted descent probe through the atmosphere of Venus, returning the first direct images of the planet's surface since 1982. A second mission, Venus Emissivity, Radio science, InSAR, Topography, And Spectroscopy (VERITAS), will follow with a launch in November 2032 to map the Venusian surface by radar from orbit. The European Space Agency is building another orbiter, Envision, for launch to Venus in 2032. The Venus armada might get started as soon as next year, when Rocket Lab aims to launch a privately funded probe to search for signs of organic material in the planet's clouds. title: Mexico to regulate violent social media content, require age verification
body: Earlier this month, two former school students murdered a vice principal and attacked students at a Mexican secondary school in Torre n, Coahuila. Authorities say they were inspired by violent and extremist content online. Today (Oct. 14), Mexican president Claudia Sheinbaum signed a presidential decree barring social media and streaming platforms from displaying or recommending violent content to teens. The order places limits on content that "generates or promotes" hate speech, extremism, sexual exploitation, suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, cyber-bullying, and other illegal conduct, according to Mexico News Daily . SEE ALSO: What 'The Social Reckoning' misses about Meta Like other social media safety bills, the decree also requires platforms verify user ages and institute parental controls. Companies have one month to get their platforms in compliance with the new law. If they fail to make changes, Sheinbaum said she will fast track a second law outlining punishment for offenders. In September, Sheinbaum announced new nationwide education rules that included a bell-to-bell cellphone ban and restrictions on tablet use across Mexico's public education system. Similar phone bans have been implemented at the state and district-level in the United States, but federal leaders have yet to enact sweeping legislation regarding device use. title: Schools across US protest FCC plan that could disconnect kids from Internet
author: Jon Brodkin
body: Schools and libraries from around the US pleaded with the Federal Communications Commission to drop the idea of ending E-Rate, a $2 billion-a-year program that connects students and library visitors to the Internet. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr has criticized school districts for having "experimented with a massive increase in screen time for students," and said E-Rate expanded too far beyond its original purpose of "supporting basic Internet access to schools and libraries for educational purposes." In June, Carr led a 2-1 vote to issue a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) seeking public comment on whether E-Rate should be "limited or sunset to reflect today’s extensive connectivity rates." Carr's proposal could result in E-Rate cutting the discounts that schools and libraries receive for telecom services and equipment, and imposing more restrictions on how E-Rate money can be used. title: Hood Warfare 2, a $5 gang shooter on Steam, is going viral
body: A $5 first-person shooter called Hood Warfare 2 has gone from near-obscurity to one of Steam s most talked-about releases in less than a week. Given the nature of the game, however, it's also drawn scrutiny for its content, its anonymous developers, and the creators who've played it live on stream. Made by an anonymous dev team called TrapStar Games, Hood Warfare 2 is a gang-themed, multiplayer Call of Duty clone set in "the streets" of Chicago, Illinois. Like Call of Duty , it has killstreaks, including a "drive by" and a "snitch," its version of the UAV drone. According to SteamDB data , it peaked at about 53 concurrent players on its Oct. 8 release day. Its player count climbed steadily before spiking past 11,700 on Oct. 12, with its all-time peak now at 15,258 as of this writing. By Steam s standards, that is a modest hit. The game's peak rank is around 1,151st all-time on SteamDB, and its current player count of roughly 4,000 puts it at 239th. Still, if Gamalytic's data is to be believed, Hood Warfare 2 has grossed $1.1 million with 219,000 units sold . As you can tell from the title, the game is a sequel. TrapStar released Hood Warfare , a Detroit-based shooter, in 2023 to little fanfare, with an all-time Steam peak of 68 players. Hood Warfare 2 caught on in a big way thanks to a deluge of content creators and streamers amused by the exaggerated stereotyping of Black American gang culture. body: IMSA provided accommodation so Ars could attend the Petit Le Mans. Ars does not accept paid editorial content. The rising tide that has been the Drive to Survive effect has lifted more boats in motorsport than simply Formula 1’s. Sportscar racing is enjoying its own surge in popularity internationally at races like Le Mans in France, but also in North America in IMSA’s WeatherTech Sportscar Championship. For one thing, multi-hour, multi-class racing lends itself better to the age of streaming and second screens than it did linear broadcast TV, and fans are taking advantage of that: IMSA’s audience grew by more than a third domestically and almost a quarter internationally last year. Having some of the coolest-looking cars racing today certainly helps, whether that’s the (mostly) hybrid prototypes or the GTs, racing versions of road-going cars from Porsche, Ferrari, and others. And it definitely helps that fan access at the races is virtually unmatched, with open paddocks and grid walks that now see huge crowds get up close to the cars just before the start of each race. “I think we're just scratching the surface,” said IMSA President John Doonan. “I think besides the people that are here on the ground, the people watching, people engaging with us on social media, I'm seeing the passion come out more. Just on the grid walk, these fans coming up and being so excited to be here.” The series has certainly been making an effort, among other things getting local high school students exposed to the industry and starting a partnership to train more mechanics with ASE. While some GTA 6 fans appeared to have bought into the memecoin in an attempt to hit Cyberleek's goal, $7.8 million is still far short of the $30 million the leakers wanted. title: Greta Gerwig channels Bowie in psychedelic The Magician's Nephew trailer
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Director Greta Gerwig could have made pretty much any movie she wanted after 2023's Barbie racked up nearly $1.5 billion at the box office. She chose to make Narnia: The Magician's Nephew for Netflix, an adaptation of C.S. Lewis' sixth novel in The Chronicles of Narnia series. Gerwig has said little publicly about the film, other than she was inspired by 1960s-era David Bowie, although she said it would not be a musical. Netflix just released the trailer, set to "Stairway to Heaven," and it's quite the wild psychedelic ride. The first book in the series, The Lion, the Witch, and the Wardrobe , was published in 1950, and Lewis did not initially intend to write any more Narnia adventures. But then an acquaintance asked how the London lamppost ended up in the middle of Narnia's woodland, and Lewis was intrigued enough by the question to start a prequel, The Magician's Nephew, in order to find an answer. Lewis found it difficult to finish the book, however, writing four other Narnia books first before completing The Magician's Nephew in 1955. There have been several adaptations, in various media, of The Chronicles of Narnia , most recently the early 2000s film franchise adapting the first three novels in the series. Those films showed diminishing returns, however, and by 2011 the film rights had expired. There were initial plans to adapt the fourth novel, The Silver Chair. Read full article Comments

body: Aaron Sorkin, famed writer of The West Wing and Academy Award-winning The Social Network, is notoriously verbose. He has a reputation for linguistic flairs that some find awkward, and many find deeply compelling. But in The Social Reckoning , a follow-up to the 2010 tale of Facebook's founding, he is uncharacteristically sparing. Yes, Sorkin who wrote and directed the new movie crams the script with one-liners and existential metaphors, random pop culture references, and cries for change, but it's what he leaves out that viewers should pay attention to. "That's why we're launching Bumble Handles." SEE ALSO: The 10 best hookup apps of 2026: I swiped until my thumb hurt Verified Bumble users can create a custom handle to easily tell people to "Find them on Bumble." But making one is optional, and users can opt out of being discoverable by their handle at any time. Exact handle names are required to search, and according to Wolfe Herd, "Discoverable doesn't mean accessible." While another user can express interest after finding someone else's profile, mutual interest is still required to start a conversation. Bumble's moderation guidelines apply when creating a handle, and the app stated it has put additional protections in place to reduce misuse, such as impersonation. This is the latest in big changes that have come to the app this year, including how men can message women first in heterosexual matches. Yesterday, Bumble announced a deal to be acquired by Ithaca Holdings for $1.3 billion , and co-CEOs Ravi Gupta and John Hegeman have taken over from Wolfe Herd. title: Global smartphone market sinks to lowest level in 14 years
body: RAMageddon is showing no sign of stopping, if the global smartphone market is to be believed. A new report from Counterpoint , a market research firm, indicates that global smartphone shipments were down 20 percent year-over-year in the third quarter of 2026. According to Counterpoint, they hit the lowest level measured since 2012, which was a time when smartphones were still not quite as prevalent in everyday life as they are now. The explanation, according to Counterpoint, is that "relentless increases" in memory prices have "significantly disrupted" shipments from manufacturers like Samsung and Apple . SEE ALSO: Apple TV 4K: Where to buy the 4th generation of Apple TV As a result, those companies have passed rising costs onto consumers, resulting in a 20 percent rise in smartphone retail prices in 2026. Per Counterpoint's research, this has led to customers holding onto older phones for longer and prioritizing high-end devices more than they might otherwise. Samsung, for what it's worth, seems to have weathered the storm a little bit, with its market share increasing to 23 percent. Counterpoint attributes this to steady demand for the mid-range Galaxy A-series and high demand for premium devices like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . Apple, meanwhile, also saw an increase in market share, while suffering a 22 percent decline in shipments year-over-year. Counterpoint theorizes that this had to do with the lack of a base iPhone 18 model in September; Apple is widely expected to launch that phone in early 2027 instead.

title: Researchers use AI to design proteins that cut up other proteins
author: John Timmer
body: A protein is a chain of amino acids held together by what are called peptide bonds. On their own, those bonds are extremely stable; they're estimated to have a half-life of several hundred years. But in Earth's environment, most proteins don't last nearly that long. That's because organisms have evolved a handful of ways to catalyze the break-up of peptide bonds, which have diversified into countless specialized protein-digesting enzymes. Proteases are everywhere and generally make short work of any proteins that find their way into the environment. Now, researchers have basically short-circuited the diversification process, using AI-based protein design tools to take the catalytic core of two types of protease and replace the entire rest of the protein. The resulting enzymes could be tuned to cut specific proteins in half, and the researchers demonstrated their effectiveness by using them to cut proteins associated with neurological diseases. Cutting proteins The basic peptide bond isn't especially interesting-looking—it's what you get when you link an amino group to an acid, releasing a water molecule in the process. As their name implies, amino acids have both an amino and an acid group, allowing them to form peptide bonds on two sides of the amino acid. This is critical for building up the long chains found in proteins. (The amino acids also have side chains with distinctive chemistry, which gives a backbone specific properties.) title: Google poisoning search results for AI scrapers, rank trackers, new report claims
body: Is Google purposefully serving up false data to AI scrapers? According to a new report from Nozzle , a search engine results page (SERP) monitoring firm, Google may be deliberately manipulating search results that are visible to rank-tracking tools and other automated services. SERPs are the pages Google displays in response to a search query. Companies often pay service providers like Nozzle to monitor these results and track how their websites rank for targeted keywords. While monitoring Google SERPs, Nozzle discovered evidence that the search giant appeared to be deliberately poisoning results pages accessed by rank trackers. Google has little apparent reason to serve misleading data specifically to these tools, suggesting that legitimate SEO services may be caught in the crossfire of Google's efforts to disrupt data scraping by AI bots . For its report, Nozzle analyzed 27.5 million SERPs and found that more than 660,000 keywords were associated with poisoned results pages. According to the report, approximately 8 percent of SERPs were poisoned. The altered results appeared in both desktop and mobile versions of Google Search. SEE ALSO: Google upgrades its AI detection tool. How to use SynthID. What does a poisoned SERP look like? According to Nozzle, it looks much like a normal search results page. However, links that typically rank well in legitimate results may be replaced with less relevant or less accurate results, often from social media platforms. "The Character.ai platform remains up and running," the statement added. Character.AI estimated both its assets and its liabilities at between $50 million and $100 million, TechCrunch reported . title: Recording device hidden in toilet paper found in top-secret OpenAI meeting room
author: Ashley Belanger
body: It took OpenAI two days to notice that a recording device was hidden in a restricted executive conference room where leadership met to discuss highly confidential information, including technical progress, government engagements, and commercial partnerships. Only those with special clearance are supposed to access that room. But the FBI believes the recording device was planted by Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old engineer from Saudi Arabia, who became a permanent US legal resident in 2020. In a press release Tuesday announcing his arrest, the FBI alleged that chatbot logs and CCTV footage suggested that Alfozan—who worked as an OpenAI engineer for more than a year—sought to use the device to spy on OpenAI and risked leaking trade secrets in a way that threatened national security. To conceal the USB device, Alfozan allegedly wrapped it in toilet paper, then plugged it into the back of a conference room television. The device was likely planted on September 28, and OpenAI found it on September 30 and quickly determined that its contents were encrypted, the FBI said. Days later, on October 5, OpenAI installed a camera in that conference room, and the CCTV footage allegedly showed Alfozan attempting to retrieve the recording device that same day. title: Legendary FPS level designer Richard "Levelord" Gray dies at 68
author: Kyle Orland
body: Prolific first-person shooter level designer Richard "Levelord" Gray died Monday at the age of 68, based on reports shared on social media by Apogee Entertainment yesterday. He had "dealt with cancer on and off for a while now," according to former colleague Joe Siegler . After studying computer engineering in the '80s and tinkering on some early games in COBOL, Gray broke into the industry at the age of 35 in 1994 with the launch of GrayDoom , a set of four maps for the then-new Doom that were widely shared on CompuServe and beyond. The work attracted the attention of Q Studios' Nick Newhard, who contracted Gray to work on level design for the late '90s cult classic Blood . Gray was subsequently hired by 3D Realms, where he said he was given free rein in designing "half the levels" for Duke Nukem 3D . There, he was also responsible for the famous, signed "You're Not Supposed to Be Here" easter egg , which players could find only by using cheats to explore outside of the usual confines of the map. title: GTA 6 file size leak: Cyberleek reveals eye-watering storage requirements
body: The person leaking a bunch of gameplay videos of Grand Theft Auto VI may have just revealed the most useful information in all of their leaks. On the Cyberleek website (per our colleagues at PCMag ), one of the latest updates included a threat to release a full build of the game in some form if people on the internet raised the leaker's crypto memecoin to a $30 million market cap. The coin has since crashed and looks like it's not going to get anywhere close to that level, but more importantly, the update included a file size for the playable build they have evidently been taking clips from: 200GB. SEE ALSO: When will 'GTA 6' launch on PC? We may have good news. That's obviously a huge number, and makes up more than 20 percent of the usable storage space on a base PS5 or Xbox Series X console. Perhaps surprisingly, it's not as big as some other games, as recent Call of Duty titles clear 200GB by a good margin. But it would still be one of the biggest single-player file sizes we've seen yet, and speaks to the scale and scope of GTA 6 . Of course, this should be taken with at least a tiny bit of skepticism. We don't know much about the build Cyberleek has been leaking footage from. If they do indeed have the full game on hand, it could be an older build that hasn't been fully optimized yet, so the true GTA 6 file size could theoretically be smaller once the actual game comes out on Nov. 19. But you better start clearing up some space ASAP regardless. Want to learn more about getting the best out of your tech? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories and Deals newsletters today.

title: The most exciting part of the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake has nothing to do with playing the game
body: Nintendo is closing out its 2026 Switch 2 first-party release calendar with a full remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , and everyone has something to say about the way it looks. But what about the way it sounds ? I got to play around an hour of the upcoming remake, which launches on Nov. 5, at a recent press event. While there's plenty to say about the visuals and gameplay, I wanted to take a moment to focus on the soundtrack. Just like with the Switch 2 Star Fox remake that released earlier this year, perhaps my most anticipated aspect of this take on Ocarina is the prospect of having a fully orchestral version of every song on Ocarina 's brilliant, timeless musical score. I'm glad to say that, based on what I heard, this is exactly what I wanted. Ocarina of Time 's new soundtrack is gorgeous In the demo, I got to check out four areas that have notably memorable themes in the original game: Kokiri Forest Hyrule Field Hyrule Castle Town The Forest Temple Each theme in the remake was true to the original, as Nintendo swapped out the synthesized instruments for their real-life counterparts. So far, none of the music I've heard has strayed too far from the direction of the original, so don't expect a sudden burst of electric guitar in the boss fights or anything like that. That said, the Castle Town theme did have an added layer of ocarina, which is appropriate. What's here is both respectful of the original vision and, frankly, sounds a little better to my ears, as a guy who prefers real instruments to their MIDI variants. title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time is my favorite video game ever. After playing the remake, I get the vision.
body: As fun as it is to be an iconoclast at times, one of my most basic opinions is that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Nintendo 64 is one of the all-time greats. There is, of course, a rose-colored tint to that take. Seeing the vast, explorable world of Ocarina for the first time as a child is basically why I love video games now. I was so taken with the idea of looking out onto an expansive horizon and knowing that anything could be out there that I became obsessed with the medium and, well, now I play video games for work. It hit me at just the right time in my life to make a permanent impression on me, and I'm still chasing the high of the first time you step out onto Hyrule Field to this day. All of that is to say I should, in theory, be as scrutinous as anyone regarding the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 . But after playing it for about an hour at a recent Nintendo press event, I came away confident that there is a vision here beyond just "let's remake an old Zelda game so we have something to market alongside the upcoming movie." title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
author: Dan Goodin
body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet-of-things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered. Still, the results do raise concerns about the possibility of new forms of computer worms. Challenging to shut down Anthropic further warned not only about the new potential malware, but also that it could be difficult to stop. In its blog post, it wrote that “a replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days). Unlike non-AI malware, it could also figure out unfamiliar devices on its own.” Read full article Comments

title: The Internet’s undersea backbone is slipping into the danger zone
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: Despite the expansion of Starlink and other communications satellite services, most of the world’s Internet traffic still travels through subsea cables crisscrossing the ocean floors. Those fiber-optic cables coexist with a network of oil and gas pipelines and submarine power cables—and all these crucial links connecting countries and continents now face growing sabotage risks as gray-zone warfare and open conflicts have become widespread. The rising risks to the world’s invisible infrastructure beneath the waves are the main subject of a new book by Elisabeth Braw , a senior fellow at the Atlantic Council who leads the Threats to the Global Maritime Order Initiative . Her book, titled Undersea War , explores the modern rise in suspicious incidents in which ships dragging their anchors for unusually long periods have cut or damaged undersea cables and pipelines from the Baltic Sea to the Pacific Ocean. Braw acknowledges that about 60 percent of undersea cable damage is primarily due to human error during fishing and shipping activities, when weighted nets or anchors drag across the seabed. Natural hazards such as storms and undersea landslides also account for a smaller proportion of such incidents. In total, between 150 and 200 cables are damaged each year and usually repaired quickly. Read full article Comments

title: For the first time, scientists catch shifting clouds on an alien world
body: Astronomers have watched Earth-like clouds drift and shift on a cold, distant world, the first time they've seen that beyond our solar system. The world, WISE 0855, lies 7.5 light-years away in space . Astronomers classify it as a brown dwarf , something that is too large to be a gas giant planet but too small to burn like a star. Though WISE 0855 doesn't have much in common with our planet, it does have clouds made of water like Earth's. Using NASA 's James Webb Space Telescope , a team led by University of Arizona astronomer Brittany Miles observed those clouds thicken and thin in real time, while gases welled up from deep inside it. An atmosphere is often the only part of a distant world astronomers can study, and much of what they hope to learn depends on interpreting it correctly: what it's made of, what's happening deep beneath its clouds, and how it compares with the worlds that orbit the sun . But clouds and weather constantly reshape the light that reaches a telescope, underscoring how important it is for astronomers to understand them or risk misreading the world underneath. "Before JWST, we only had photometry, which mixed up the effects of clouds, chemistry, and temperature all together," Miles said in a statement. "Now we can actually distinguish them." title: Martin Shkreli livestreamed himself violating lifetime pharma ban, FTC says
author: Beth Mole
body: Martin Shkreli—the ex-pharmaceutical executive infamous for illegally hiking the price of a lifesaving anti-parasitic drug by more than 4,000 percent and getting a seven-year prison sentence for the fraudulent scheme he used to do it— has been under a lifetime ban from the pharmaceutical industry since 2022. However, according to the Federal Trade Commission and the attorneys general of seven states, Shkreli has "flagrantly and repeatedly" violated that ban nearly the entire time—allegedly by trading stock in dozens of drug companies and discussing the industry during livestreams on social media. On Tuesday, the FTC and the seven states asked a federal judge to hold Shkreli in contempt for the alleged violations. The states include New York, California, Illinois, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Virginia—the same states that joined the FTC in suing Shkreli in 2020 over the "elaborate anticompetitive scheme" involving the anti-parasitic drug, Daraprim. The scheme raised the price from $17.50 per pill to $750 per pill virtually overnight, while blocking generic competitors from entering the market. Read full article Comments

title: An AI image of Mia Goth sparks Instagram fan account controversy
body: AI-generated images can now give celebrities entire social media moments they never took part in. For Mia Goth, that meant a supposed response to her divorce right down to a T-shirt and breakup soundtrack. After news of the Pearl and MaXXXine actress's divorce filing from Shia LaBeouf a few weeks ago, an Instagram post appeared to show Goth wearing a shirt that read "MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN." Paired with Beyonc s "Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)," it was easy to read as a comment on the split. Except Goth s representative says the image was AI-generated. And Goth doesn t even use social media. The post came from @miagoth_ , a verified fan account with more than a million followers. Despite the fan-page label, People initially wrote about the image as a selfie Goth had posted herself, describing the shirt as her fashion choice days after filing for divorce. (The article and post have both been removed.) SEE ALSO: Taylor Swift's wedding photos are going viral. There's just one problem. That confusion is exactly what the actress's team says it has been trying to stop. "Mia Goth does not have ownership of, nor does she engage in social media on any platform," her representative, Christine Tripicchio, told The Verge . "We have filed multiple complaints with Instagram to remove the verified fan account which continues to post counterfeit, AI images of Mia Goth." Tripicchio also questioned how the account had qualified for a verification badge in the first place. title: ESA targets Anbernic emulation handhelds as "superfake" piracy enablers
author: Kyle Orland
body: For years, Chinese hardware manufacturers have carved out a market niche with an array of handheld Android gaming devices focused on retro emulation and/or more modern game-streaming capabilities. Now, though, a major game industry trade group is targeting one of those manufacturers, Anbernic, asking the US Trade Representative (USTR) to add the company to its list of "Notorious Markets" that "engage in or facilitate substantial copyright piracy or trademark counterfeiting." TorrentFreak was among the first to notice the request from the Entertainment Software Association (ESA), which was submitted to the USTR last week. In it, the US trade group—which represents major publishers including Nintendo, Microsoft, PlayStation, Amazon, Epic, EA, Ubisoft, and more —notes that Anbernic devices "are routinely offered or shipped with removable memory cards preloaded with hundreds or thousands of unauthorized copies of copyright-protected video games published by ESA members." While many online sellers do include an SD card full of ROMs alongside emulation hardware of all types, Anbernic itself does not appear to do the same when selling directly from its website. Regardless, the ESA argues that these ROM-laden Anbernic devices selling through "normal retail channels" help to "normalize hardware-based piracy by delivering illicit catalogues through a polished consumer product." This, the ESA says, meets the threshold for a "superfake," an ill-defined designation that applies to "high-quality counterfeit trademark goods ... on a commercial scale." Read full article Comments

title: Musician Raye reveals the scale of reseller AI bots buying up concert tickets
body: Raye is a British singer-songwriter who planned on holding an intimate one-night concert for her fans next week. The event's venue has capacity for 5,000 attendees. There were 1.8 million sign-ups for tickets. It sounds like a good problem to have, right? Having that many fans? One problem. The vast majority of those sign-ups were AI bots, according to Raye, run by profit-seeking resellers hoping to make money off her fans. "This Symphony May Contain Hope" is a planned one-night live concert by Raye at the Royal Albert Hall in London on Oct. 23. It appears the singer was expecting to receive thousands of sign-ups and then send out a pre-sale link for interested parties, with tickets available on a first-come, first-served basis. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. However, Raye wasn't expecting the resellers and AI bots to hit as hard as they did. "Sadly our sign-up process was overwhelmed by scalpers, using AI bots to create hundreds of thousands of fake registrations," Raye wrote on her X account. "It's a new world we are living in now, I have never witnessed bots on this scale." "It is so important to me that fans can be tickets at the face value price," she continued. Raye says that for this special event only, she and her team would manually review the sign-up list and send a pre-sale link and code to individuals that they believe are real fans. Google first announced Argon on Sept. 30 in a blog post by Google DeepMind SVP Koray Kavukcuoglu. At that point, it was limited to trusted cyber defenders in Google s Fairwind Program. With today s release, Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can use Argon in the Gemini app. Google says Argon is built for long, complex work in software engineering, enterprise knowledge work like legal and finance, and cybersecurity defense. For everyday chat, Google says the model gets to the point with less hedging, repeats itself less, and avoids clich s. On longer tasks, it gives more frequent progress updates. Argon 4 arrives during a busy fall season for frontier AI models. Google repeatedly missed its own deadlines for the launch of Gemini 3.5 Pro , and meanwhile, Anthropic released Claude Opus 5.5 , and OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra . Meta's "super intelligence" Muse Wonder was just released yesterday. As expected, Google s own evaluation shows Argon testing ahead of its rivals on many benchmarks. title: Tinder hadnt updated most AI scam detection models in years, Senate report finds
body: On Tuesday, Democratic Sen. Maggie Hassan released the results of her investigation into romance scams on Match Group apps, including Tinder and Hinge. Hassan, the New Hampshire Democrat who serves as ranking member of the Joint Economic Committee, began this investigation in Sept. 2025, when she and Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn sent a letter to Match and its CEO, Spencer Rascoff, requesting documents about romance scams on the company's platforms. SEE ALSO: AI romance scams: Follow these tips to avoid being scammed online These scams occur when a bad actor gains someone's trust by pretending to be romantically interested in them, only to then ask for money. The Federal Trade Commission reported that Americans lost almost $1.5 billion to romance scams last year. The investigation called "Outmatched: Tinder, Scammers, and Match Group's Efforts to Catch Up" focused on how the company detects and removes scam accounts. As part of it, Match Group provided the committee with two written responses and internal documents in Oct. and Nov. 2025, and additional documents throughout this year. Match Group's senior vice president of trust and safety, Yoel Roth, also sat down for an interview with committee minority staff in April 2026. The investigation found that, as of the second half of 2025, Tinder hadn't updated most of its AI models used to detect scammers and other bad actors for years. title: The Paris Auto Show is full of interesting cars Americans can’t have
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: Perhaps the days when auto shows debuted new models aren’t entirely over. The big trade shows for cars were a gateway drug for many, expos where you could see the newest models of today and the concepts of tomorrow. But automakers increasingly got tired of sharing the spotlight with each other. New reveals moved offsite to events the night or even the week before the show itself. One by one, brands pulled out of auto show after auto show until there was little left to see . And then the pandemic hit. But the news out of Paris, where its auto show held media day yesterday, seems like we stepped back into a time when automakers would debut new cars aplenty. That retro vibe extends to the cars themselves, with plenty of familiar nameplates reimagined. France’s Renault has a long and glorious history of delightful concept cars, and more on what it brought to Paris later. But the star of the show was arguably Stellantis, with strong work from Citroen, Peugeot, and Fiat, to name but three. But this article is meant to irritate you, because I’m pretty sure none of the stuff you’re seeing here will come to the United States. And it’s doubly irritating considering what Stellantis’ brands do offer us over here, doubling down on the same malign trends I saw back in 2020 : did you know they’re about to relaunch a V8 Hellcat-powered Charger ? The announcement, part of a slate of press releases stealth-dropped by Apple (following one brief tease from Greg "Joz" Joswiak , Apple Senior Vice President of Marketing), includes a new smart display called Apple HomeView , a second-generation HomePod mini , a fourth-generation Apple TV 4K , and the Apple Home Collection , a line of smart security cameras, thermostats, and a door lock built with LG Electronics and Schneider Electric. Unlike previous Apple smart home products, all of the new releases lean on Siri AI, the rebuilt version of Siri that Apple is now bringing to its home devices. Strangely, Siri AI will not be available at launch on the new HomePod mini 2, but only in a future update. The announcements were not a total surprise. Bloomberg's Mark Gurman has reported for months on what to expect from Apple's October releases, and the HomePod refresh was the most anticipated piece. It is the first new HomePod hardware in roughly three years, since HomePod (2nd generation) arrived in early 2023, and the first update to the HomePod mini since the original launched in 2020. Notably, the M6 MacBooks that many observers expected this month were absent. Gurman has indicated they're still set for release in October, however. For now, the company is focusing on the smart home, a category where Amazon and Google have long set the pace. title: Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google has already added a few AI features to the Play Store, but a lot more are coming . The previously released Ask Play feature is expanding to offer more AI-powered discovery options in Google's app store, and Google is also using AI to build a recommendation engine called Game Finder. For people who have embraced AI to build their own apps, the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations. Google rolled out Ask Play in 2025 as a small chatbot interface on Play Store listings. It lets you ask questions about an app or game, either by typing it in manually or choosing from a list of suggested queries. Starting today, Ask Play is expanding into a more general way to search for apps and games. You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon. Google's other AI discovery announcement focuses on games. The new Game Finder feature leans on all the usage data Google's app platform has hoovered up over the years, featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA. Read full article Comments

title: What is bloomscrolling? Meet doomscrolling’s happier alternative.
body: It's a classic tale: You open Instagram for a break, and 20 minutes later, you re caught up on three arguments, worried about something you hadn't heard of til this morning, and wondering why you picked up your phone in the first place. Then a video of a puppy appears, and for a few seconds, things improve. Or at least they feel that way. That kind of detour has a name: bloomscrolling. Bloomscrolling is defined as actively seeking out uplifting, calming, or inspiring content (nature footage, funny clips, stories of people helping one another, etc.) instead of letting one distressing post lead to the next (otherwise known as doomscrolling ). SEE ALSO: I stopped doomscrolling after the election. You should too. Think of it as opening an app with a positive destination. Maybe you want underwater footage of an Australian coral reef, an artist s process, or the latest update from someone whose elderly dog has a devoted following. Whatever the subject, you re choosing something you enjoy rather than waiting to see what turns up. And you don t have to abandon the news to make room for this type of content. As neuropsychologist Sanam Hafeez told Real Simple , "[Bloomscrolling] does not mean pretending that bad things are not happening or completely avoiding the news." "It is more about creating a healthier balance so that everything you see online is not making you feel anxious, angry, or overwhelmed," she says. title: They war-gamed dimming the Sun. It went even worse than you think.
author: Karl Mathiesen, WIRED.com
body: When it comes to deciding the fate of the planet, Colleen Golja always thought science and reason would have a seat at the table. That was until one morning last September in London, when the climate researcher took part in the first in a series of war games. The goal: to prevent an uncontrolled global race to develop a technology aimed at cooling the planet but that comes with vast, unknown risks that could reshape life on Earth. “I thought that would be such an easy thing. Like, we can all agree to do ethical research and make sure it's for the better of all humans,” she told WIRED. “And boy, was I wrong.” The simulation, titled Exploring Geopolitical Tipping Points and Climate Cooling Strategies, saw a couple dozen foreign-relations experts, scientists, military personnel, and former government officials from across the world convene in a meeting room at Queen Mary University of London. After making introductions over coffee and little yogurts, they sat at tables arranged in a square with the name of the country or organization each person was playing: national governments, climate NGOs and nonprofits, indigenous groups, and tech companies. Golja was assigned to provide technical advice to help participants make scientifically literate decisions. Read full article Comments

title: High-speed video reveals how honey bee stingers pump venom
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: Credit: Ramirez-Esquivel et al 202 Credit: Ramirez-Esquivel et al 202 Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom. Honey bees ( Apis mellifera ) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee's stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. But the precise mechanism by which the pumping action is achieved has never been directly observed. Read full article Comments
